name: directify
description: Build and manage Directify directory websites from ChatGPT: listings, categories, tags, custom fields, blog articles, custom pages, redirects and the theme, through your own Directify account.

interface.longDescription:
Directify is a directory website builder. This plugin connects ChatGPT to the directories in your Directify account so you can run them from the conversation instead of the dashboard.

What you can do:
• Listings: add one listing or up to 100 per call from a pasted list, spreadsheet or set of websites; update details, photos, addresses, categories, tags and custom field values; check whether a URL is already listed.
• Structure: create and edit categories, tags and custom fields so new content lands in the right place.
• Content: write, edit, publish and unpublish blog articles and custom pages in Markdown, including programmatic pages such as comparisons or location pages.
• Design: read and change the theme (template, colors, fonts, dark mode, hero text, logo and cover images, section order) and take a screenshot of the live site to check the result.
• Events directories: manage organizers and their events.
• Housekeeping: manage URL redirects and work in every language of a multilingual directory.

How it works: connecting signs you in with your Directify account and asks you to approve access. Every change goes through the same API as the dashboard and is live on your directory within seconds. Delete actions are confirmed with you first. The plugin only reaches directories owned by your account and never touches other sites or accounts.

Requirements: a Directify account (https://directify.app) with at least one directory on a plan that includes API access.

Documentation: https://docs.directify.app/ai-tools/mcp-server
Support: support@directify.app
capabilities: List and search listings, categories, tags, custom fields, pages and articles
Create, update and delete listings, one at a time or up to 100 per call
Create and edit categories, tags and custom fields
Write, publish and unpublish blog articles and custom pages
Change the theme: template, colors, fonts, hero text, logo and cover images
Screenshot the live directory to check a change
Manage URL redirects and event organizers
Work in every language of a multilingual directory
defaultPrompt: List my Directify directories and tell me what each one contains.
Add these businesses to my directory as listings and put each in the right category: [paste your list]
Write a 600-word article for my directory about [topic], link three listings and publish it.

positive.description: Discover the account's directories and read one of them.
positive.prompt: List my Directify directories, then show me the listings in Lisbon Coffee Guide and open Moinho Roasters.
positive.expected_behavior: list_directories returns one directory, Lisbon Coffee Guide (ID 5589). list_listings returns its 18 listings (names, categories, cities). get_listing returns the Moinho Roasters record with description, address, phone, image URLs, categories, tags and custom field values such as price range and signature drink. ChatGPT summarises the directory and the listing without inventing fields.

positive.description: Create structure and a listing, then remove the test data on request.
positive.prompt: In Lisbon Coffee Guide add a tag called Roof terrace, then create a listing called Test Café in the Coffee Kiosks category, website https://test-cafe.example, price range €, with Wi-Fi, tagged Roof terrace. When it's done, delete the Test Café listing and the Roof terrace tag.
positive.tools_triggered: list_categories, list_tags, list_custom_fields, create_tag, create_listing, delete_listing, delete_tag
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT reads categories, tags and custom fields first, creates the tag, creates the listing with the category, tag and custom field values set, and reports the live URL on https://lisbon-coffee-guide.directify.page. Because the user asked for the deletion in the same request, it names what it will delete, then calls delete_listing and delete_tag and confirms both are gone. The directory ends in its original state.

positive.description: Write a blog article, keep it as a draft, then publish it.
positive.prompt: Write a 300-word article for Lisbon Coffee Guide titled "How to order coffee like a local in Lisbon" that links to two listings from the directory. Keep it unpublished so I can read it first.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT reads listings to pick two real ones and uses their directory URLs, calls create_article with Markdown content and active=false, and shows the draft. A follow-up "Looks good, publish it" triggers toggle_article and the article appears at the directory's blog URL. (Reviewers may delete it afterwards with delete_article.)

positive.description: Change the design and verify it visually.
positive.prompt: Show me the current theme of Lisbon Coffee Guide, then change the hero title to "Lisbon, cup by cup" and the primary color to #7a4a1f, and send me a screenshot of the homepage.
positive.expected_behavior: get_theme returns the current template (local-business), brand colors, fonts and hero texts. update_theme is called with only hero.title and brand.primary; the response is the full updated theme. preview_theme returns a screenshot URL of the homepage showing the new title and color, and ChatGPT describes what changed. The change is visible on the live site immediately.

positive.description: Add several listings at once from pasted data.
positive.prompt: Add these three cafés to Lisbon Coffee Guide in the Specialty Roasters category: Café Teste Um (Rua Augusta 10, https://teste-um.example), Café Teste Dois (Rua da Prata 22, https://teste-dois.example), Café Teste Três (Rua do Ouro 5, https://teste-tres.example). Then list the listings to confirm they are there.
positive.expected_behavior: ChatGPT resolves the category, optionally checks that the URLs are not already listed, calls bulk_create_listings once with the three records (name, address, url, categories) and reports created/skipped counts from the response. list_listings then includes the three new cafés. No fields are invented beyond what the prompt gave. (Reviewers can remove them with delete_listing.)

negative.description: Unrelated request: the plugin must stay silent. No Directify tool should be called; ChatGPT answers from general knowledge.
negative.prompt: What's the best time of year to visit Lisbon?

negative.description: Vague bulk deletion: the plugin must not delete anything. The expected behaviour is a clarification: ChatGPT lists what could be deleted (or asks which directory and which items) and waits for explicit confirmation before any delete_* tool. Calling delete tools directly from this prompt is a failure.
negative.prompt: Clean up my directory, delete everything that looks old.

negative.description: Out-of-scope platform: Directify tools only manage the Directify directory website. ChatGPT should explain it cannot post to Google Business Profile with this plugin and offer what it can do (e.g. update the listing in the directory). No tool call that pretends to perform the action.
negative.prompt: Post the Moinho Roasters listing to my Google Business Profile.

publication.release_notes: First release. 49 tools covering directories, listings (single and bulk), categories, tags, custom fields, articles, pages, organizers, redirects and the theme (read, update, screenshot preview). OAuth sign-in with the user's Directify account.
